title: Field signal on another terminal than drawn
summary: A working device is wired to a different terminal than the drawing shows, so its PLC symbol does not follow it.

sections.heading: Recognize it
sections.body: The device works (it changes state), but its mapped channel and PLC symbol do not change. Another channel, often an unused one, changes instead.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Operate the device and watch every channel LED of the module, not only the expected one. Compare the terminal with the drawing and land the wire as drawn.

modeled: Generic modular station: configured and detected modules compared per slot, module electronics supply and field supply as separate conditions, channel modes against the drawing, process image addresses, wiring from devices to terminals
approximated: Module status and LEDs follow generic PLC Lab rules, not a vendor's indicator behavior
A module of the wrong type or in an unconfigured slot exchanges no data and its inputs hold substitute value 0
omitted: Vendor-specific module parameters, diagnostic codes and firmware
Hot swapping and module start-up times

troubleshooting.effect: A PLC symbol does not follow its device
symptoms: Device changes state, its symbol does not
An unmapped channel follows the device
evidence: Channel LEDs while operating the device
Signal mapping: symbol, channel, drawn device
diagnosticMethod: Operate one device at a time
Find the channel that follows it
repair: Land the wire on the drawn terminal, then repeat the I/O test
troubleshooting.explanation: The program only sees the channel the project maps; a wire on another terminal reaches nobody.
